market_question: Will the US acquire part of Greenland in 2026?
reasoning: The US acquiring part of Greenland by end of 2026 is highly improbable. Denmark has consistently refused to sell or cede territory, and no serious negotiations are underway. A use-of-force scenario would be an extreme departure from norms and alliance commitments, making a 13.5% market price far too optimistic. A 1% true probability still accounts for unforeseeable black-swan events.
evidence_points: Trump repeatedly expressed interest in buying Greenland, but Denmark's Prime Minister called the idea 'absurd' and rejected it.
Greenlandic and Danish officials have consistently stated the island is not for sale and sovereignty will not transfer.

Historical precedent: US territorial acquisitions since 1900 (e.g., American Samoa, Virgin Islands) were consensual purchases from willing colonial powers; no modern case of acquiring territory from a NATO ally.
sources_consulted: Official statements from Danish PM Mette Frederiksen (2019, 2025)
US State Department remarks on the US consulate in Nuuk (no mention of sovereignty)
News archives on Trump's Greenland interest (Reuters, AP)
